notes.s: The first fan song: no promise of a perfect road, only a wish for more good days.
notes.t: BTS's first official fan song, on 화양연화 Young Forever in 2016, written at the hinge where years of being dismissed turned into their first award wins. The opening refuses the standard idol promise outright, and the second verse answers critics in their own voice before thanking them for the proof. The bridge is the group admitting they hid the ugly parts because they were too inexperienced to show them, and thanking ARMY for carrying the tears anyway. The subtitle is the line fans quote, and the 하나 둘 셋 count is the live chant, so in concert the crowd supplies the numbers. It is the traditional last song of a BTS show.
k: A fixed Korean blessing, walk only on the flower path, meaning may you have nothing but good times ahead. Fans say it to idols constantly and idols say it back. Opening the fandom's own song by refusing to say it is the entire thesis of the song.

A sentence that stops at -기를 and never supplies a verb is a wish left deliberately hanging, the shape of a prayer or a toast. The missing ending is roughly 바란다, I hope. This is why the subtitle feels cut off in English and why it cannot be fixed in translation.

The specific insecurity that makes a person belittle someone else. Not envy, which sits in the envier quietly; this word names the smallness in the one doing the sneering, which is what makes thanking them for it a put-down rather than grace.

花樣年華, the time of life in fullest bloom, the title of the album era this song closes and borrowed from the Wong Kar-wai film known in English as In the Mood for Love. Calling ARMY the flower of 화양연화 hands the fans the thing the era was named after.
